# glinet_wireguard_server (Resource)

Manages the configuration and the options of the WireGuard server of the router (`wg-server.set_config` and `wg-server.set_setting` in the router API). The router has one WireGuard server, so use one instance of this resource. The server always exists on the router, so create takes over the server. When the server is not initialized, create initializes it (`wg-server.generate_key`), as the "initialize" button of the web UI does: the router makes the keys of the server. The initialization cannot be undone. While the router reports the server as not initialized, the resource does not exist. Each attribute that is not set keeps the value of the router: the provider sends back the value that it reads from the router just before the write. The provider sends the configuration call only when `address_v4`, `address_v6`, `listen_port` or `private_key` differs, and the options call only when an option differs: on create from the values of the router, on update from the state. The web UI permits a change of the configuration only while the server is stopped, so a configuration write fails while the server runs or starts; stop the server in the web UI first. The resource does not start or stop the server. Use `glinet_wireguard_server_peer` for the peers and `glinet_wireguard_server_route` for the route rules. With a configuration that has an IPv6 address, the provider sends `ipv6_enable` with the value of the last read, as the client does. Firmware 4.8.3 does not give `ipv6_enable`, so the provider then sends `false`; the web UI of firmware 4.8.3 does not send it, and what the router does with it is not known. The state keeps the private key as clear text; protect the state. Import the server with the ID `wireguard_server`. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Initializes the WireGuard server when it has no keys, and keeps the private key of the router.
# The server must be stopped for a change of address_v4, address_v6, listen_port or private_key.
resource "glinet_wireguard_server" "this" {
  address_v4       = "10.0.0.1/24"
  address_v6       = "fd00:db8::1/64"
  listen_port      = 51820
  client_to_client = false
  local_access     = true
  masquerade       = true
  mtu              = 1420
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `address_v4` (String) IPv4 address of the server in the tunnel with a prefix length, for example `10.0.0.1/24` (`address_v4` in the router API). It must be a private address, and the prefix length must be 30 or less. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `address_v6` (String) IPv6 address of the server in the tunnel with the prefix length 64, in `fd00::/8`, for example `fd00:db8::1/64` (`address_v6` in the router API). `""` removes the address, as the web UI sends it for an empty input; what the router does with `""` is not known. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `client_to_client` (Boolean) Whether the peers can reach each other (`client_to_client` in the router API). When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `listen_port` (Number) UDP port of the server, from 1 to 65535 (`port` in the router API). When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `local_access` (Boolean) Whether the peers can reach the LAN of the router (`local_access` in the router API). When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `masquerade` (Boolean) Whether the router translates the source address of the traffic of the peers (NAT) (`masq` in the router API). When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `mtu` (Number) MTU of the tunnel, from 68 to 65535, or `0` for no MTU value (`mtu` in the router API). The web UI sends `0` for an empty input; what the router does with `0` is not known. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) Private key of the server, 44 characters of base64 (`private_key` in the router API). When it is not set, the router value does not change. The provider never sends an empty key, because it is not known what the router does with it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `wireguard_server`.
- `public_key` (String) Public key of the server, which the router gives from the private key (`public_key` in the router API).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "wireguard_server".
terraform import glinet_wireguard_server.this wireguard_server
```
